description: Join us for an evening deep dive into React Server Components. We'll cover the mental model shift, practical patterns, and how RSCs change the way we think about data fetching. Beginners welcome!
locationNotes: Take the elevator to the 2nd floor, turn left at the reception desk.
announcement: Pizza and drinks provided courtesy of our sponsor, Acme Corp!

description: We'll walk through building beautiful, production-ready command-line tools using Typer for argument parsing and Rich for terminal output. Bring your laptop and follow along!
locationNotes: Enter from Camp St, head up to the 3rd floor via the main staircase.

description: How do you build a design system that developers will actually use? This talk covers token architecture, component documentation, and the organizational buy-in strategies that make or break adoption.
locationNotes: Event is in the back bar room. Ask the bartender to point you toward the tech meetup.

description: A hands-on session covering rolling updates, blue/green deployments, and canary releases in Kubernetes. We'll demo real failure scenarios and how to recover gracefully.
Generics are one of TypeScript's most powerful — and most misunderstood — features. This workshop breaks them down with progressive examples, from basic constraints to conditional types.
locationNotes: Elevator access available near the Camp St entrance.
announcement: Bring a laptop — this is a hands-on session.

description: Retrieval-Augmented Generation sounds great in demos — but what breaks in production? We'll cover chunking strategies, embedding model selection, vector DB trade-offs, and evaluation techniques.
announcement: Panel format — three speakers from local AI teams will present and take questions.

description: asyncio, aiohttp, and async generators — this talk goes past the hello-world examples and into the patterns you need for real networked applications. Intermediate Python experience recommended.
locationNotes: Back bar room, same as last time. Look for the laptop stickers.

description: We'll take a real, publicly available website and audit it for WCAG compliance together in real time. You'll leave knowing how to use axe DevTools, screen readers, and color contrast checkers in your own workflow.
Logs, metrics, and traces — done right. This session covers instrumenting a Node.js service with OpenTelemetry, shipping data to a collector, and making sense of it all in Grafana.
locationNotes: We'll be in the main bar area this time, not the back room.
announcement: Live demo environment will be provided — no local setup required.

meetupName: Fine-Tuning vs. Prompting: When to Use Each
description: A practical comparison of fine-tuning open-source models versus prompt engineering with frontier models. We'll look at cost, latency, accuracy trade-offs, and walk through a real use case from a local startup.
announcement: Guest speaker from a local AI startup will be joining for the second half.
